verdicts.reason: ChainID names a gas-station chain, not a product; 233 small integers nesting inside a 1..591 product sequence is coincidental overlap and there is no chains table for it to point at.
Exact name match, transactions naturally reference customers, and the sample values (31543, 46707, 7654) look like customer identifiers drawn from a 32k-row customer table.
Exact name match, a transaction happens at a gas station, and the spread of source values (3704, 656, 1152) across the 5716 stations reads as real identifiers.
Exact name match and a transaction buying a product is the obvious designed relationship; only 28 distinct products in a 1000-row sample is normal for fuel/shop purchases.
Exact name match, monthly consumption rows per customer, and 30566 of 32461 customers covered with high spread is exactly what a designed reference looks like.
Products' own key 1..591 nesting inside transaction ids 1..1000 is the classic two-surrogate-sequences false positive; a product does not point at a transaction.
